latest_nl_proof:
Let A_r be the set of all s in S congruent to r modulo m. Since the complement of S in N_0 is finite, there exists an integer N such that every n >= N lies in S. Fix r in {1,...,m-1}. Choose an integer t with r + tm >= N. Then r + tm belongs to S, so A_r is nonempty. Because A_r is a nonempty subset of N_0, it has a least element; by definition this is w_r. Since w_r is congruent to r modulo m, there exists an integer k_r with w_r = r + m k_r. If k_r = 0, then w_r = r, which is a positive element of S smaller than m, contradicting that m is the multiplicity, that is, the least positive element of S. Hence k_r >= 1, so k_r is a positive integer.

Now fix integers i,j with 1 <= i <= j <= m-1.

If i + j < m, then i + j is in {1,...,m-1}. Since w_i and w_j belong to S and S is closed under addition, w_i + w_j belongs to S. Also w_i + w_j is congruent to i + j modulo m. By minimality of w_{i+j} among elements of S in that residue class, w_i + w_j >= w_{i+j}. Writing each w_t as t + m k_t, we get
(i + m k_i) + (j + m k_j) >= (i + j) + m k_{i+j}.
Cancelling i + j gives m(k_i + k_j - k_{i+j}) >= 0. Since m > 0, it follows that k_i + k_j >= k_{i+j}.

If i + j > m, then 1 <= i + j - m <= m-1, so w_{i+j-m} is defined. Again w_i + w_j belongs to S, and it is congruent to i + j - m modulo m because i + j and i + j - m differ by m. Therefore, by minimality of w_{i+j-m} in that residue class, w_i + w_j >= w_{i+j-m}. Substituting w_t = t + m k_t gives
(i + m k_i) + (j + m k_j) >= (i + j - m) + m k_{i+j-m}.
Rearranging gives m(k_i + k_j + 1 - k_{i+j-m}) >= 0. Since m > 0, we obtain k_i + k_j + 1 >= k_{i+j-m}.

These are exactly the inequalities asserted in the lemma. Therefore the tuple (k_1,...,k_{m-1}) satisfies the Kunz inequalities.
role_in_parent: Shows that every numerical semigroup of multiplicity m determines an admissible Kunz vector.
statement_nl: Let S be a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m >= 2. For each r in {1,...,m-1}, let w_r be the least element of S congruent to r modulo m, and write w_r = r + m k_r with k_r a positive integer. Then the tuple (k_1,...,k_{m-1}) satisfies the Kunz inequalities: for all integers i,j with 1 <= i <= j <= m-1, if i + j < m then k_i + k_j >= k_{i+j}, and if i + j > m then k_i + k_j + 1 >= k_{i+j-m}.

domain_restrictions: S is a numerical semigroup: S ⊆ ℕ0, 0 ∈ S, closed under addition, and ℕ0\S is finite
m is the multiplicity of S: m = min(S\{0}), with m ≥ 2

Residue-class definition requires that for each r ∈ {1,...,m-1}, the set { s ∈ S : s ≡ r (mod m) } is nonempty and has a least element (implied by the numerical semigroup/Apery-set property, but not stated explicitly)
For each r ∈ {1,...,m-1}, w_r is the least element of S with w_r ≡ r (mod m)
Integers i,j satisfy 1 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ m-1
Case split is only for i+j < m and i+j > m (no explicit inequality stated for i+j = m)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Given any numerical semigroup S with multiplicity m ≥ 2, define for each r ∈ {1,...,m-1} the least element w_r ∈ S such that w_r ≡ r (mod m), and set k_r ∈ ℕ by w_r = r + m k_r (so k_r > 0). Then for all integers i,j with 1 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ m-1: (a) if i+j < m then k_i + k_j ≥ k_{i+j}; (b) if i+j > m then k_i + k_j + 1 ≥ k_{i+j−m}.
quantifier_order: For all numerical semigroups S with multiplicity m ≥ 2
For each r ∈ {1,...,m-1}, define w_r as the least element of S with w_r ≡ r (mod m) and write w_r = r + m k_r
For all integers i,j with 1 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ m-1
If i + j < m then (inequality 1 holds)
If i + j > m then (inequality 2 holds)

variables.domain: S ⊆ ℕ0 and S is a numerical semigroup (0 ∈ S, closed under addition, and ℕ0\S finite)
variables.name: S
variables.role: ambient object; semigroup from which witnesses w_r and values k_r are derived

variables.name: m
variables.role: multiplicity of S; also modulus for residue classes

variables.name: r
variables.role: residue-class index defining w_r and k_r

variables.domain: w_r ∈ S and w_r ≡ r (mod m)
variables.name: w_r
variables.role: least element of S in the residue class r modulo m (a witness depending on S and r)

variables.domain: k_r ∈ ℕ and k_r > 0, defined by w_r = r + m·k_r
variables.name: k_r
variables.role: Kunz coordinate corresponding to residue class r

variables.domain: i ≤ j ≤ m-1 (and hence 1 ≤ j ≤ m-1)
variables.name: j

witness_dependencies: w_r depends on (S,m,r) via w_r = min{ s ∈ S : s ≡ r (mod m) }
k_r depends on (S,m,r) via k_r = (w_r − r)/m
The inequalities depend only on the resulting tuple (k_1,...,k_{m-1})
